inference (v1, author): Files A, B and C record activity on one host (IEWIN7) in one Sysmon log; A and B involve the same remote peer 10.0.2.19. C is NOT shown to involve that peer.
confidence_v1: Medium (same host/log); Low (same actor across A-B-C)
alternative_anticipated_by_author: Three separate lab test runs by the dataset author that share a VM, not one intrusion.
discriminating_evidence: C has no network event to 10.0.2.19; logon IDs: A=0x3e7 (SYSTEM), B=0x1d313d (IEUser), C=0xffe4 (IEUser processes) and 0x3e7 (SYSTEM service VSSVC); the two IEUser sessions differ, and 0x3e7 is the shared SYSTEM session, which does not identify an actor; 11 and 315 record IDs are missing between files.
cannot_be_shown_by_these_logs: Whether one operator ran all three; why records were omitted.

inference (v1, author): At 20:26:51 a remote client at 10.0.2.19 created a service named "hello" over SMB (\ntsvcs pipe) whose ImagePath launched hidden PowerShell (PsExec-style remote execution).
confidence_v1: High (service + command line); Medium (that T01 caused T03)
alternative_anticipated_by_author: Authorised remote administration or software deployment that happens to use a service and PowerShell.
discriminating_evidence: ImagePath uses -nop -w hidden -noni plus a compressed/base64 loader; link T01->T03 rests on a 335 ms gap, not a shared session ID.
cannot_be_shown_by_these_logs: Which account authenticated (no Security 4624/7045 events in the sample).

inference (v1, author): The second PowerShell process (pid 2484) opened an outbound TCP session to 10.0.2.19:4444, consistent with a reverse shell / C2 channel.
alternative_anticipated_by_author: A benign test listener on port 4444; "meterpreter" appears in the FILE NAME, which is a label, not evidence.
discriminating_evidence: Process GUID/pid of T07 matches T09; destination is the same host that initiated the SMB session (T01).
cannot_be_shown_by_these_logs: Payload content and any data sent over the channel (no packet capture).

inference (v1, author): T08 (access mask 0x1fffff, pid 3872 -> 2484) shows process injection.
alternative_anticipated_by_author: Normal parent-to-child handle: CreateProcess gives the parent a full-access handle to the child it just started.
discriminating_evidence: T07 records pid 3872 (the T06 process) as parent of pid 2484, started 391 ms after T06; SourceImage field in T08 is truncated ("50\Windows\...") so the record is imperfect.
cannot_be_shown_by_these_logs: Whether any memory was written into 2484 (Sysmon event 8/25 not present).

inference (v1, author): T10 (service "hello" Start set to 4 = disabled) shows the actor cleaning up persistence.
alternative_anticipated_by_author: Tool or Service Control Manager changing state as part of normal service lifecycle; no key-delete event exists.
discriminating_evidence: Only a value change is logged, 1.2 s after T03; no registry key deletion (Sysmon 12) in the sample.
cannot_be_shown_by_these_logs: Whether the service key still exists after the session.

inference (v1, author): At 20:32:51 a remote WMI session (WmiPrvSE parent) ran whoami /all as IEWIN7\IEUser, redirecting output to \\127.0.0.1\ADMIN$\__1556656369 (Impacket wmiexec-style discovery).
alternative_anticipated_by_author: An administrator running a WMI management script with output redirected to ADMIN$.
discriminating_evidence: Output file name __1556656369 decodes to 20:32:49 UTC, matching T11 (20:32:49.659), so the sender and this host clocks agree to about 1 s.
cannot_be_shown_by_these_logs: How IEUser credentials were obtained (no logon events).

inference (v1, author): At 22:49 msiexec launched C:\Windows\Installer\MSI4FFD.tmp, which spawned cmd.exe; the same cmd.exe (pid 2892) ran whoami 3 min 18 s later, suggesting an interactive shell.
alternative_anticipated_by_author: A legitimate installer custom action. Counter-signal: the binary's PE description says "ApacheBench", a mismatch with spawning cmd.exe.
discriminating_evidence: T25 parent pid 2892 equals T24 pid 2892 (verified). The 3 min gap fits a human operator but also a timed script.
cannot_be_shown_by_these_logs: Who started msiexec, and how the MSI reached the Temp folder (no file-create event in the sample).

inference (v1, author): T18 and T20 (Sysmon event 2, "file creation time changed") show timestomping of the MSI.
alternative_anticipated_by_author: Normal Windows Installer behaviour: caching the package to C:\Windows\Installer preserves the original creation time (22:43:38.892).
discriminating_evidence: Both events show the same CreationUtcTime for the same package; copy-with-preserved-time is the simplest explanation.

inference (v1, author): T19 (VSSVC.exe started by services.exe seconds after msiexec began) indicates shadow-copy tampering.
alternative_anticipated_by_author: Windows Installer commonly triggers Volume Shadow Copy for restore points; no vssadmin/delete command appears.
discriminating_evidence: No command line other than the service itself; no deletion event.
cannot_be_shown_by_these_logs: Whether any snapshots were created or removed.
